# Echoes of Spira: actions and implementations ledger

<!-- Generated by tools/actions-ledger.mjs from docs/target/actions.json. Edit the data, not this file. -->

The central record of everything **done** on the project since it began on 2026-09-15: what was built (implementations, art installs), what was carried out (deploys, reviews, records, infrastructure, account moves, downloads, maintenance, process changes), who did it, which decisions it carried out, and the evidence. Its sibling ledgers are `CHANGELOG.md` (player-facing, one entry per live build) and `DECISIONS.md` (Bailey's decisions, `docs/target/decisions.json`). Dates are Eastern time. The project began as Pyrefly Reprise and is called Echoes of Spira since 2026-10-04; internal names keep "pyrefly".

Rows group sensible units of work, never one row per commit: a feature lane, a fix batch, an art install, one deploy, one review, one clean-up. "Who" names Bailey, the driver session (the main chat that plans and coordinates), a lane (a sub-agent doing one track), a side session or an outside session. Evidence that exists only in the driver's own notes is marked "(not in the repo)".

## How to add a row

1. Append one line to the `actions` array of `docs/target/actions.json` (one entry per line; never edit, reorder or renumber an old row; the next id is the last id plus one, even when the work is older):

   `{"id":"A-0000","date":"YYYY-MM-DD","kind":"deploy","title":"...","what":"...","who":"...","decisions":["D-000"],"game":"both","result":"...","evidence":["commit abc1234"],"reversible":{"value":true,"how":"..."}}`

2. Run `node tools/actions-ledger.mjs` to regenerate this file. `node tools/actions-ledger.mjs --check` exits 1 when the data is malformed or this file is stale; `tests/unit/actions-ledger.test.ts` runs the same checks.
3. `kind` is one of `implementation`, `art`, `deploy`, `review`, `records`, `infrastructure`, `account`, `download`, `maintenance`, `process`. `game` is `FFX`, `FFX-2`, `both`, `n/a` (decided from the sources, AGENTS.md rule 14). `decisions` links the D- (and early E-) ids the row carries out. `result` says whether it is done, shipped in which release, on a branch, parked, reverted or failed and why.
4. The repository is public: no email addresses (write "account #1", "#2" or "#3"), no card or payment details, no account ids, tokens or keys, no other personal projects, nothing else private to the owner. The validator refuses an email address, a 32-character hex id and card-like digits.

- **A-0498** · `implementation` · both · **r394-headlock phase 1: the engine holds every registered head to the idle's size on screen at a pose swap (branch r394-headlock, tip 2a1af1f5, pushed; 48 new tests, the full suite passing; phase 2 owed; both games)**
  - What: Carries out D-510 (his "Engine keeps the head steady (Recommended)": the fix for the Chapter V and XVII knock-out swaps that CHK-026 still catches), restarted at 00:51:24 EDT when D-519 lifted PROTECT mode (A-0487 had parked it). A lane (sub-agent, Sonnet) worked about 49 minutes, light work only (no build, browser or harness). Branch r394-headlock from origin/r393-int b80f772f, four commits, game case both: 242d748e (the paper preflight, docs/plans/r394-headlock-review.md), ff209ae7 (310 head boxes added to the generated tables, 36 subjects, emitted from the record's own boxes), 34cc3e7e (the engine and its tests) and 2a1af1f5 (the handoff, docs/handoff/r394-headlock.md). Design: every plane with a registered head is scaled about its feet each frame so its head box, projected through that frame's camera, is as big as the idle's under the same transform (one correction step, clamped to 0.9 to 1.1; the clamp is reported through actor.headLock.snapshot() and one console warning per actor and pose); where there is no head box, no camera, the idle itself, another figure's painting or a stand-in, the scale is bit-identical to before; ?headlock=off switches it off for same-build A/B; the hidden Leblanc chapter is not locked (its rows carry no head box). Code: src/engine/HeadLock.ts, HeadLockStage.ts, PaintedActor.holdHead and one call in BattlePresenterStage.ts. Checks: tsc clean, pose-scale-check passes, no new orphan, the full suite once, 911 files and 13,523 tests passed, 48 new tests in five files; across 274 registered poses at four cameras the median ask was 0.5 percent and the largest 8.8 percent, no clamp hit; the pass costs about 2.2 microseconds per actor per frame.   - What: Branch r39-color (ef0868b5) took the bloom's light back off a figure in the grade, so the switch gives true colour without the glow the old colour path hid; it was merged into r391-int at efc4bf1d, and commit ffb048c0 turned FIGURE\_TRUE\_DEFAULT from 0 to 1 as Bailey picked (D-437, decision A of the morning brief). The renderer reads the start amount through figureTrueFromAddress(search), so ?figtrue=0 or \_\_pyrefly.fx.figureTrue(0) puts release 39's look back. The finding behind it: the colour chain never applied the sRGB encode, so every painting was drawn with its gamma applied twice; with the encode the figures reproduce their paintings to a mean CIEDE2000 of 2.5 to 3.7, against 12.9 to 15.9 before. Costs he accepted: figures read paler and calmer, Bahamut's wings go from deep red to the painting's salmon; his dark body also lifts toward charcoal and that part stays open. Backdrops, floors and effects keep today's look. Both games: shared rendering, measured in FFX Chapters I and III and FFX-2 Chapters IV and VI.

The lane (branch r391-reach, a bug fix inside approved scope) solves lunge(distance) at action start against the picture: each figure's painted front is read row by row from its alpha through the camera the blow is seen through, and the lunge is the smallest distance (never less than today's, at most +3 world units) at which the fronts overlap by 14 px; the extra distance rides an eased step so the jerk rule is not tripped; release 39's Chapter III special case (the staging row's follow flag) is gone. Game case from the sources: the FFX party and fiends reach (FFX has no run-in, D-354 holds one for Bailey); an FFX-2 girl reaches after her run-in (research/ffx2-combat-core.md: a short-range dressphere runs in) but a long-range girl does not (she fires from where she stands); FFX-2 fiends were a judgement call the sources do not settle, flagged to Bailey and answered in D-461. - **A-0452** · `implementation` · both · **Lane r391-stalls: masters upload to the graphics card ahead of their frame in bands, so no master swap lands mid-turn (both games)**
  - What: Release 39 swapped a 2x, 3x or 4x master into a painting's texture in place and Three uploaded it inside the next render: 145 ms for a 4096-square figure master and 193 to 216 ms for a 5376 x 3072 backdrop, on the frame that drew it; a pose never drawn before paid the same at its first draw. The lane (branch r391-stalls from release 39; paper preflight docs/plans/r391-stalls-review.md first, because the change is deep-class) decodes the master off the main thread, uploads it ahead in row bands of 1.3 to 1.7 ms and lets the painting adopt the finished GL texture between two draws (Three's Source sharing). A warm pool uploads paintings before their first draw (capped at the smaller of 640 MB and 30 percent of the class's texture budget), a slow call over 6 ms cuts the next 8 frames' budget to a quarter, ?stage=off is the kill switch and WebKit keeps the old path. Measured on the production code in headless GPU Chromium, the first three real-key turns at 1440p of Chapters I, IV and VIII: GL texture calls over 5 ms 18, 11 and 12 down to 1, 0 and 0; frames over 50 ms that carry an upload 13, 9 and 8 down to 4, 0 and 0. Level 0 of every governed texture is byte-identical to the legacy upload; on screen 0 to 311 of 3.69 million pixels differ, by at most 1 of 255. Costs: Chapter I's first menu holds 1,338 MB of textures against 715 MB, and the first sharp master lands from 1.4 s earlier to 1.0 s later. The frames still over 50 ms are CPU tasks in the game's own tick, not uploads. Both games: shared plumbing, nothing reads a game id.
  - Who: lane sub-agent (Sonnet) under the driver session · Decisions: D-385, D-440
  - Result: done on branch r391-stalls (94e01a00), merged at e37c2df4 and live in release 39.1; the deep review saw the fix hold in Chapters I, Anima and Trema but not lower the FFX-2 slow frames in Vegnagun and Fallen Aeons

Root cause by running the engine: GradeShader is the composer's last pass, a raw ShaderMaterial with no colour-space fragment, and the composer's targets are linear, so the sRGB encode is never applied and every painting's gamma is applied twice; with every pass neutral and the encode added, 11 of 11 figures reproduce their painting to median dE00 0.8 to 2.4 (8.5 to 23 without). F plus, CAS and the hi-res tiers are not causes. In the repo: a default-OFF switch (?figtrue=0..1 or \_\_pyrefly.fx.figureTrue), 0 of 3,686,400 pixels differing with it off; on, figures show their painting's colour, take no bloom and have their rim cut, which is paler and calmer than today (Bahamut's wings go from deep red to dusty salmon).   - What: Because release 39's standard view was not visibly sharper (A-0388), a lane built the options on branch crisp-options and measured real frames at 1440p and 4K against live: A as built, B MSAA, C SMAA with sharpening, D supersampling 1.5x to 2x, E prefiltered mips with anisotropic filtering, F the best mix. Findings: release 39 draws SMAA twice (the MAX-mix pass before the grade and the renderer's pass after it), so one SMAA is +19 percent detail for free; a 3x supersample holds 2.0 times release 39's fine detail, so the screen and not the files is the limit; the plates' anisotropy of 8 never reached the GPU (now 16). Recommended F plus: 2x supersample with a Lanczos-3 resolve before the bloom, both SMAA off, sharpening 0.3 before the grade, plates anisotropy 16, a step-down to F by device class and frame time, phones keep today's frame: 100 percent of the ideal's detail (release 39 as built 50, live 64) for +2.0 ms at 1440p and +4.7 ms at 4K.
